currentContext.expansion: NFL's largest expansion is the Namrup-IV brownfield Ammonia-Urea complex at Namrup, Assam, taken forward through the joint venture company Assam Valley Fertilizer and Chemical Company Limited (AVFCCL) incorporated on 25.07.2025 with the Government of Assam (40%), NFL (18%), OIL (18%), HURL (13%) and BVFCL (11%); the plant will have annual urea production capacity of 12.7 LMT, tentative CAPEX of Rs 10,601.40 crore, NFL equity contribution of around Rs 572.45 crore, and a tentative schedule of 48 months to mechanical completion and commissioning. Domestically, NFL is planning a 25,000 MTPA Bentonite Sulphur plant at its Vijaipur Unit at an estimated cost of Rs 104.03 crore with an implementation period of about 14 months, and — following Department of Fertilizers direction — two commercial-scale Sulphur Coated Urea (Urea Gold) plants of 250 MTPD at Nangal and 300 MTPD at Vijaipur, with PDIL being lined up as Project Management Consultant. Completed or in-progress smaller projects include the Agro-chemical plant at Bathinda at an approximate cost of Rs 12.57 crore (production commenced from three of five trains, one under rectification and one under completion by the contractor), the 5,000 MTPA Urea Gold R&D plants at Panipat and Nangal costing Rs 3.43 crore and Rs 6.52 crore respectively (desired R&D results not achieved; Nangal under modification and Panipat equipment planned for use as spares at Nangal), the doubling of the Vijaipur bio-fertilizer plant from 700 MTPA to 1,400 MTPA during FY 2025-26, and the completed ERP implementation. On renewables, a 1500 kWp grid-connected rooftop Solar PV plant at Panipat (total capex Rs 6.67 crore including GST) has slipped from December 2025 to an expected August 2026 completion, and rooftop solar plants of 1735 kWp, 600 kWp and 1220 kWp are planned at Nangal, Bathinda and Vijaipur respectively; a 300 KW rooftop solar plant already operates at Vijaipur. Integrated energy-saving projects continue: Topsoe-recommended schemes are being implemented phase-wise starting with the synthesis gas compressor and steam turbine drive revamp at Nangal, Bathinda and Panipat, while Saipem-recommended schemes for Vijaipur-I & II remain to be implemented. Overseas, NFL with RCF and Indian Potash Limited has a strategic collaboration with Uralchem JSC to explore a 2 million MT per annum urea facility in Russia, currently at feasibility-study stage. The Directors' Report states CAPEX achievement of Rs 247 crore excluding capital work in progress in 2025-26.

capex_expansion.body: NFL's largest expansion is the Namrup-IV brownfield Ammonia-Urea complex at Namrup, Assam, taken forward through the joint venture company Assam Valley Fertilizer and Chemical Company Limited (AVFCCL) incorporated on 25.07.2025 with the Government of Assam (40%), NFL (18%), OIL (18%), HURL (13%) and BVFCL (11%); the plant will have annual urea production capacity of 12.7 LMT, tentative CAPEX of Rs 10,601.40 crore, NFL equity contribution of around Rs 572.45 crore, and a tentative schedule of 48 months to mechanical completion and commissioning. Domestically, NFL is planning a 25,000 MTPA …

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- Large player in domestic Urea production
- Pan-India distribution and sales network, leveraged for trading and other businesses
- Multi-product company with well established "Kisan" brand (except for subsidised fertilizers)
- Majority equity held by Government of India (74.71% through the President of India), a Central Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers
- Three plants located in the most intensive fertilizer-consuming states, i.e. Punjab and Haryana
- Manufacturing facilities for industrial products
- Well established eco-system for seed production and sale, …

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Management flags this as a major risk with severe financial impact: tightening of energy norms has reduced operational profit from the urea manufacturing business, mainly at the Vijaipur-I unit, and further reduction in energy norms shall make operations unviable. NFL has already spent more than Rs 1000 crore to meet revised norms, and the Vijaipur-I norm extension carries a 35% penalty on the difference between revised and tentative norms. Norms are under further review, with DoF revising the New Energy Norms applicable from 01.04.2025 to 31.03.2028.
- Identified by the Risk Assessment and Risk Management Committees as a major risk with severe financial impact on production. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East disrupted international prices of natural gas, ammonia, urea and phosphatic fertilizers and raised freight and logistics costs, and lack of availability of domestic gas with an increasing trend in RLNG prices adversely impacts urea manufacturers' profitability.
- Urea is sold at a GoI-controlled price and the business depends on subsidy; delay in receipt of subsidy leads to higher interest cost. Implementation of DBT changed subsidy payment from supply to sale, aggravating the working capital problem. Short-term borrowings rose to Rs 3,959.25 crore as at 31.03.2026 from Rs 1,995.77 crore a year earlier, mainly due to the high cost of imported P&K fertilizers.
- Listed as both a weakness and a risk. Urea MRP is fixed by GoI and is highly inadequate relative to current cost of production or imported price; the Government has not yet considered raising the minimum fixed cost of Rs 2,300 per tonne of Urea, which is affecting the viability of some units including Vijaipur-I. Deletion of the minimum fixed cost provision retrospectively w.e.f. 02.04.2014 for Vijaipur-I is separately flagged.
- These plants consume higher energy than new and large-capacity plants, structurally disadvantaging them against the tightening energy norms and raising the cost of production.
- Explicitly flagged in MD&A Risk & Concerns; constrains NFL's ability to fund equity participation in domestic and overseas fertilizer companies and its own expansion programme at a time when the debt equity ratio has risen to 1.39:1 as on 31.03.2026 from 0.72:1.
- MD&A lists recruitment of manpower to meet the shortfall arising out of massive retirements and future growth, and rationalisation of manpower, as risks and concerns; permanent employee turnover was 13.72% in FY 2025-26.
- The chemical fertilizer industry operates in a hazardous environment and faces risks related to health, safety and environment in addition to general business and financial risks; the Company handles hazardous substances such as liquid ammonia and chlorine gas and carries Extended Producer Responsibility obligations for roughly 16,000 metric tonnes of plastic waste annually under the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Maximise Urea production in an energy-efficient manner, keeping consumption within the Target Energy Norms under NUP-2015
- Maximise production of industrial products including Ammonium Nitrate and Nitric Acid
- Maximise production of Bentonite Sulphur and bio-fertilizers
- Produce new products such as Sulphur Coated Urea (Urea Gold) and agro-chemicals
- Import and sell fertilizers such as Urea, DAP, MoP, complex fertilizers and water soluble fertilizer including Calcium Nitrate
- Expand domestic trading of agro products — pesticides, weedicides, compost, water soluble fertilizers, Calcium Nitrate, …

themes.title: Fertilizer subsidy & nutrient-policy cycle
themes.need: Fertilizer makers are driven by NBS/urea subsidy policy, gas-pooling and nutrient pricing rather than the crop-protection volume/molecule-launch recovery. Q1FY27's supply-side read comes from MBAPL: revenue roughly flat at INR 416cr with EBITDA +16% and PAT +17% purely on cheap March-bought raw material that management said is now EXHAUSTED, with utilisation only ~43-45% because of raw-material availability rather than demand - SSP sales were +28% and NPK +33% YoY against production down 7%/28%. Its Dhule (Maharashtra) integrated complex commissions +3,30,000 MTPA DAP-NPK plus 99,000 MTPA phosphoric acid in Oct-2026 and a second phase in Oct-2027, framed as a >50% turnover jump toward ~INR 3,500cr revenue and 15.6 lakh MT capacity by FY28; Egypt/Jordan rock-phosphate sourcing (non-Hormuz) insulated it relative to import-dependent peers. Subsidy clarity and gas costs still set the near-term margin.
themes.driver: NBS/urea subsidy policy (the Oct-Mar rate revision), gas-pooling and nutrient pricing; MBAPL's Oct-2026 Dhule commissioning and the utilisation ramp toward ~90%; kharif demand pull-through after a delayed monsoon.

hero.oneLiner: National Fertilizers Limited is a Government of India-controlled central public sector fertilizer company operating five gas-based Urea plants, with the Government of India holding 74.71% of its paid-up share capital.
